data.title: Nearly 50% rise in drug seizures by Hong Kong customs in first half of year
data.description: Hong Kong customs recorded a nearly 50% year-on-year rise in drug seizures during the first half of 2026, driven by notable increases in smuggling activities via air and sea routes.

data.title: Despite military might, Saudi struggles to crush the Houthis
data.description: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia has deep pockets and cutting-edge weapons yet for more than a decade it has been unable to quash Yemen's battle-hardened Houthis.

data.title: Inside the Venezuelan prison meant to 'drive you insane'
data.description: CARACAS - Former political prisoners of Venezuela's Rodeo I are unable to shake the memories of punishments dealt out by hooded jailers in the country's most notorious prison.

data.title: In Bangladesh, Pakistan's Jinnah photo stirs anger
data.description: DHAKA - Pakistan founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah died nearly eight decades ago, but his photograph has become the centrepiece of a fresh battle over history at Bangladesh's top university.

data.title: Two New Zealand naval ships transit Taiwan Strait
data.description: WELLINGTON — Two New Zealand naval vessels passed through the Taiwan Strait last week, the New Zealand Defence Force said Tuesday.

data.title: UK agrees to support Saudi in struggle with Houthis: reports
data.description: LONDON - British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has agreed to give military support to Saudi Arabia to help it tackle attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis, media reports said on Monday.

data.title: Macron says talks with Trump on Red Sea, Ukraine 'constructive'
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - French President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday he had positive talks with his US counterpart Donald Trump on the conflicts in Ukraine and in the Red Sea.

data.title: Trump to tout deals, defend Iran war in UN speech
data.description: UNITED NATIONS - US President Donald Trump is expected to claim he is winning both on the battlefield and as a peacemaker on Tuesday in a speech to the United Nations overshadowed by growing spillover from his stalled war against Iran.

data.title: A Cuban zoo, and its animals, in epic battle for survival
data.description: HAVANA - Every day, veterinarians and zookeepers make their way to Cuba's National Zoo by whatever means they can, determined to not abandon the nearly 1,000 animals in their care and help save species at risk of extinction.

data.title: Bardot auction in Paris fetches nearly one million euros
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - An auction of French screen legend Brigitte Bardot's personal items fetched nearly one million euros in Paris on Monday, almost 20 times the estimate, the Millon auction house told AFP.

data.title: British Museum bans photos of Bayeux Tapestry as crowds linger
data.description: LONDON - The British Museum has banned visitors from taking pictures of the Bayeux Tapestry in order to keep the crowds flowing through an unprecedented London exhibition, a spokesperson confirmed Monday.

data.title: El Nino weather pattern enters record territory: scientist
data.description: NEW YORK - The strengthening El Nino weather pattern has tied for the most intense on record on a widely-used metric, a senior scientist told AFP Monday, even as its influence is already being felt from Central America to Indonesia.

data.title: Man shot by ICE agent in Texas detained with bullet inside him: lawyer
data.description: AUSTIN - A Venezuelan national shot and wounded by a US immigration agent in Texas was jailed with the bullet still inside his body, his lawyer said Monday.

data.title: South African ostriches plucked alive for luxury fashion: report
data.description: JOHANNESBURG - South African ostrich farms are using mechanical pluckers to remove feathers from living birds destined for major luxury fashion brands in techniques that are cruel and painful, animal welfare group World Animal Protection said on Monday.

data.title: US media outlets to sue Trump administration after White House ban
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Three leading US news outlets announced Monday they will go to court after being banned from the White House, as President Donald Trump claimed that media critical of his administration is a "Cancer" threatening national security.

data.title: German auto workers stage mass protests in bid to save jobs
data.description: HANOVER (GERMANY) - German automotive workers held nationwide protests on Monday calling for government and management action to protect jobs and factories in an industry facing severe headwinds.

data.title: Supply issues, attacks on refineries driving diesel prices upward
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Prices at the pump for diesel and other fuels are hitting fresh highs in many countries as the wars and the Middle East and Ukraine have not only choked off crude supplies, but also damaged refineries, with the resulting capacity constraints increasingly being felt, according to analysis out of France.

data.title: COP31 host says AI's climate footprint to be a summit priority
data.description: NEW YORK - COP31 host Turkey said Monday that pursuing "climate-responsible AI" and pushing tech companies to power data centers with clean energy would be priorities when it stages next month's summit.

data.title: Renewables hit record in 2025, but world must move faster: report
data.description: NEW YORK - A new report has shown global renewable power capacity grew by record levels last year, with the findings hailed as a sign by the UN climate chief that the "brute power of market forces" is making the transition to clean energy irreversible.
